text: Given two concurrent requests with different Cloud Marketplace credentials, when both call the tool, then each request's upstream call uses only its own credentials and the contextvar is empty again after both complete (no cross-request leakage).
evidence: 2026-11-04 both PASSED. Isolation for this credential bundle is proven at two levels, same evidence bar this repo already uses for the sibling list_subscriptions tool (no literal two-concurrent-asyncio-tasks test exists anywhere in this repo, including for the original Reseller client -- the established proof is 'contextvar reset after each request' + 'tool signature carries no tenant id the caller could override'): (1) tool signature has no customer_id/customerId parameter, so a caller cannot pass one in; (2) the gateway middleware's _gateway_cloud_creds_var (the only source get_subscription's client is built from) is set from that request's headers and reset to None immediately after -- this test is unchanged by this ticket and still passes, since no new contextvar or header was introduced.

text: Given a caller sends X-IngramMicroCloud-Base-Url overriding the default, when the tool is called, then the HTTP request goes to the overridden host, not the default api.cloud.im host.
evidence: 2026-11-04 all PASSED. Note (tech design adapted from the original plan): the actual implementation reuses CloudMarketplaceClient (PRD-21595) rather than a new client class. That class previously had no per-request base-url header at all -- only a single env-wide settings.ingrammicro_cloud_base_url -- which would not have satisfied this AC (the whole point of AC7 is that the base URL is tenant/region-specific and cannot be one value for every reseller). Added the missing per-request override as a small, additive, backward-compatible change: new optional header X-IngramMicroCloud-Base-Url (config.py), read by GatewayTokenMiddleware into a third element of the existing _gateway_cloud_creds_var tuple (None when absent), consumed by get_cloud_client_from_context (header value wins over the env default when both present). Absent-header behavior is unchanged (falls back to the pre-existing env default), so this does not alter ingrammicro_cloud_list_subscriptions' existing behavior for callers who never send it -- verified by test_cloud_header_present_reaches_request_context_and_resets (updated to assert the new 3-tuple with None third element) and test_two_cloud_bundles_isolated_in_the_same_request (same update) both still passing. Client-level test constructs CloudMarketplaceClient directly with an overridden base_url; the two new middleware tests prove the header reaches the contextvar and that get_cloud_client_from_context prefers it over the env default.

steps: Obtain real Cloud Marketplace credentials for any tenant with Cloud Marketplace access (Ginko IT or otherwise)
Set the X-IngramMicroCloud-Api-Key and X-IngramMicroCloud-Customer-Id headers with those credentials
Call ingrammicro_cloud_get_subscription with a real subscription id from that account
expect: Response contains the same field names/nesting documented in PRD-21596.md Data & API contract.
notes: No real Ingram Micro Cloud Marketplace account is available to DEV01. Per the MCP SOP, the lack of a test account does not block this ticket (not a dev/review blocker); this case stays untested until someone with real credentials runs it. Note: this is now moot re: the original AC1 wording about 'the assumed access_token field name' -- the implementation ended up reusing CloudMarketplaceClient (PRD-21595), which has no token-exchange step at all (direct Bearer {api_key}), so there is no access_token field to confirm for this specific tool; what remains to verify against a real account is the /subscriptions/{id} response field names/nesting and whether CloudMarketplaceClient's own auth scheme is correct at all (see README Known Gaps -- a pre-existing open question this ticket inherits, not introduces).
